title: QuickCost Summary Tile — MVP slice and acceptance decision
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a minimal, high-utility ‘QuickCost’ summary tile for the Console home dashboard that gives engineers and SREs an at-a-glance cost signal by route/model with a clear degradation path. This ticket captures the scope reduction decisions, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating for the MVP slice.
problem_statement: Full cost-explorer and per-route breakdown is valuable but expensive to implement and store. We need a compact surface that communicates cost change signals and basic attribution without the full telemetry/trace integration required by the long-term vision.
proposed_mvp_scope: A single QuickCost tile on the Console home that shows: total cost delta (24h), top 3 cost-driving routes by token spend, and a single quick action link to the full cost explorer (degraded if not available).
Backend: aggregated daily and rolling-24h cost rollup computed from existing billing events; no per-request trace linking for MVP.
Frontend: compact visualization (sparkline + numeric delta) + top-3 list with small percentage bars; accessible, keyboard-navigable, responsive to smallest Console width.
Rollout: feature flag controlled, 100% internal preview for first week, then staged opt-in for pilot customers.
Fallbacks: if cost rollups are delayed, show last successful snapshot with explicit ‘stale data’ badge and support toggle to hide tile.
Telemetry: emit a lightweight tile interaction event (tile_shown, tile_click_route) for product evaluation; avoid high-cardinality labels in MVP.
out_of_scope_for_mvp: Live per-request cost streaming and tracing integration (this is a planned post-MVP capability).
Custom date range picker or drill-down views inside the tile — the tile links to the full cost explorer for that functionality.
Route-level anomaly detection or automated recommendations (future work tied to Optimize).
acceptance_criteria: Tile is present on Console home for flagged accounts and visible to internal users (QA) — UI matches approved mock in Figma (link in attachments).
Tile shows total cost delta and a 24h sparkline derived from rollup service with max 5% data mismatch tolerance vs billing dashboard for sampled accounts.
Top-3 routes by token spend are accurate within 10% for traffic levels >1000 tokens/day; routes are labeled by route ID and display short alias where available.
‘Stale data’ badge appears if the latest rollup timestamp is older than 6 hours and interaction events are emitted correctly to product analytics channel.
Feature flag exists and can be toggled without a console restart; rollout to internal preview must complete with no SLO regressions on API endpoint used by rollup service.
Accessibility: tile passes basic a11y audit (color contrast, screen-reader label for top-3 list items, keyboard focus order).
Documentation: short help text + one-pager in Confluence describing what the tile shows and limitations (link in attachments).
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: We intentionally limit rollups to daily + rolling-24h to avoid scaling the rollup pipeline for arbitrary date ranges. This reduces fidelity but enables shipping quickly.
Decision: Do not implement per-request linking to traces in MVP to avoid high-cardinality telemetry and storage costs; preference is to route users to cost explorer for deep dives.
Tradeoff: Top-3 routes is a heuristic (peak-driven); may hide smaller but growing routes — we will monitor and add growth heuristics post-MVP.
Decision: Keep interaction telemetry low-cardinality; avoid including customer IDs in tile events to respect privacy and reduce analytics cost.
Fallback plan: if rollup service cannot sustain additional queries, tile will display snapshot cache with explicit staleness messaging and an incident-runbook will be executed.
